tagline: A desert loop to a mining town that kept two graves.
intro: South of the Virgin River crossing at Riverside, Gold Butte Road runs into Gold Butte National Monument, and at Whitney Pocket, about 20 miles along, the pavement ends. Graded dirt carries on some 20 miles more to the old townsite. There the byway turns back north on Gold Butte Wash Road, narrows to a single lane and runs on to Mud Wash before it meets itself again.

The monument around it holds sandstone towers, rock art and the remains of agave roasting pits. Gold Butte had a post office, a hotel and a livery stable in its day, but the whole district produced only $75,000, and by the end of 1910 the town was abandoned.

moments.title: Whitney Pocket
moments.text: A wall of sandstone pitted with hollows of every size, worn by water and wind over millennia, stands where the pavement gives out.

moments.title: Gold Butte townsite
moments.text: Under a 5,013-foot butte of the Virgin Mountains, the mining town has come down to a couple of foundations, two graves and several old mine shafts.

moments.title: Devil's Throat
moments.text: Mud Wash Road starts out in a wide wash that leads to this 110-foot sinkhole, and just past it the byway closes its loop.

practical: The loop is rugged and needs sturdy tires and a high-clearance vehicle, above all on the last 20 miles over Gold Butte Wash Road and Mud Wash Road.

sources.label: BLM, Gold Butte Back Country Byway
